response.sql:
WITH grp AS (
  SELECT o.account_id, d.A3 AS region, AVG(o.amount) AS avg_amount
  FROM "order" o
  JOIN account a ON a.account_id = o.account_id
  JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id
  WHERE o.amount >= 2802
  GROUP BY o.account_id, d.A3
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS overall_avg FROM grp
)
SELECT g.account_id, g.region, g.avg_amount, g.avg_amount - o.overall_avg AS difference
FROM grp g
CROSS JOIN overall o
ORDER BY g.avg_amount - o.overall_avg DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Standing orders are the rows of the `order` table. The amount >= 2802 filter is applied to individual orders before grouping, and orders are joined to account and district with inner joins so unmatched rows are dropped.
If more than 10 groups tie on the difference at the cutoff, LIMIT 10 picks among the tied rows arbitrarily, because the query has no secondary sort key.
